questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The ceiling, which had cracks, caved in and several people __trapped__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'were trapped'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'were trapped' **should be used instead of '**trapped**'.
 
• Each clause needs a subject and a **verb**. In some cases, the best verb to use is a simple 'is' or 'was' (or some other form of the verb to be).
 
• In other cases, you may need to add the **main** verb, an auxiliary verb, or multiple** auxiliary verbs.**
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice.**
 
• To make a past passive form we use** was/were + past participle **of the **verb**.
 
 
• *Example: This problem** was solved** last week.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The ceiling, which had cracks, caved in and several people **were trapped.***** **

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Neither of them have / any experience / in software development.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'Neither of them have'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'Neither of them has' **should be used instead o**f 'Neither of them have'.**
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is: 
 
 
• Neither of + Plural Noun/Pronoun+Singular Verb.
 
 
• *Example*: *Neither of them looks after him.*
 
 
 
• *​*Either of + Plural Noun/Pronoun+Singular Verb.
 
 
• *Example*: *Either of them is at fault.*
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence, according to the above structures '**has**' should be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Neither of them has **any experience in software development.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Either the bear or the lion __have escaped from__ the zoo.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'has escaped from'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'has escaped from' **should be used instead of** 'have escaped from'.**
 
• We know that if two subjects are connected with 'neither...nor', 'either...or', 'not only...but also', 'or', etc. then the verb should be used according to the nearest subject of the sentence. 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Either Rohit or Rakesh **have** come. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• *Either Rohit or Rakesh **has** come. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
• In the given sentence the nearest subject is 'the lion' which is singular. Hence, a singular helping verb should be used.
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Either the bear or the lion has escaped from the zoo.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

The students / were tired / after working / at long hours.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'at long hours'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'for long hours'** should be used instead of** 'at long hours'.**
 
• We use for with a period of time to refer to duration (how long something lasts).
 
 
• *Example: We usually go there **for a couple of hours **in the evenings when it’s warm enough.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The students were tired after working** for long hours.***** **
